title: The Night Before the Wedding Locked Room Case
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Heiji, Kazuha, Kogoro, Ran, Inspector Megure) omitted by convention, except where an object they used (a decoy bag) is itself load-bearing evidence -- that object is kept and its owner noted only in attrs. IMPORTANT CORRECTION vs. the old cases/ file: the old file's murderer_id (s2, Yuji Sakuraba) is WRONG. Sakuraba is a deliberate false accusation: Heiji stages a full deduction show naming Sakuraba as the killer purely as bait (confirmed on-screen: 'it was all a trap we created with the Inspector's help'), Sakuraba is cleared moments later when Kaede reveals she was his alibi, and the true culprit -- unmasked only in the closing minutes of ep142 using the staged-bloodstain/no-blood-on-balcony contradiction plus a second trap involving a decoy bag -- is Kikuhito Morizono, the groom himself. This file uses Kikuhito (p6) as label.murderer_id, per the actual transcript, not the old file's wiki-derived guess. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed, attributed edge between the entities involved (person/location/object), sharing an `order` integer so edges belonging to the same real-world occurrence can be grouped without a reifying node. Multigraph: multiple parallel typed edges between the same two nodes are expected. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Sakuraba and Kaede are seen wearing matching pendants, clearly bought together -- the physical detail Kazuha and Ran independently notice that first reveals the two are secretly a couple.

Comparing the five suspects' physical situations -- Mikio's bad leg, Kaede's and Yurie's unsuitability, Kikuhito's declared fear of heights -- leaves Sakuraba as the only one nimble enough to have used the balcony escape route; used by Heiji to build the (deliberately false, staged) case against Sakuraba.

A bloodstain was deliberately left on the window latch, but there is no blood trace anywhere on the balcony itself -- if the killer really climbed down from the balcony in bloody gloves, some trace should be there. The contradiction proves the balcony escape was staged and the killer never left the crime-scene room at all.
